title: SLO bakeoff notes — latency vs throughput tradeoffs
content:
Topline: quick personal scratchpad for the SLO bakeoff we need to present next week. Goal is to produce a compact set of numbers and a hypothesis-backed recommendation for routing policies + quantization settings under multi-tenant bursty load. This is not polished — quick notes and stray commands.

Context and objective:
- Customers expect p99 < 350ms for normal workloads and p99 < 700ms for cost-tiering fallbacks. We want to show which config meets p99 350ms at target qps 250 (per-shard) and how much throughput we can get if we accept p99=700ms.
- Compare: baseline fp16 large model (L-v1), int8 quantized L-v1-q8, and a distilled small model (L-small). Evaluate both single-tenant and mixed-tenant (noisy neighbor) scenarios.

Environment and test harness:
- cluster: dev-gpu-pool-6 (4x A100-80GB) pinned, no auto-scale.
- runtime: local branch perf/bakeoff-2024 (PR 876).
- harness: goreplay-style generator + orchestrator that schedules Poisson arrivals with configurable bursts.
- script used: ./tools/run_bakeoff.sh --model L-v1 --qps 250 --dur 10m --arrival poisson --tenancy single --seed 42
- measurements: p50,p90,p95,p99, mean throughput, token/sec, KV-cache hit-rate, GPU util (nvidia-smi sampling), scheduler queue length every 5s.

Quick command snippets (for reproducibility):
- Run single-tenant baseline: ./tools/run_bakeoff.sh --model L-v1 --qps 250 --dur 10m --tenancy single 
- Run quantized: ./tools/run_bakeoff.sh --model L-v1-q8 --qps 250 --dur 10m --tenancy single 
- Mixed tenants (3 tenants, ratio 70/20/10): ./tools/run_bakeoff.sh --model L-v1 --tenancy mixed --mix 70,20,10 --qps 250
- Collect telemetry: ./tools/collect_metrics.sh --run-id $RID --output metrics/$RID.json

Key observations (first-pass):
1) Single-tenant, qps 250:
   - L-v1 (fp16): p50=38ms, p90=120ms, p95=210ms, p99=430ms, throughput stable at 250 qps, GPU util ~72%, KV-cache hit-rate ~12% (cold-ish).
   - L-v1-q8: p50=36ms, p90=95ms, p95=160ms, p99=290ms, throughput stable, GPU util ~59%, KV-cache hit-rate ~11%.
   - L-small: p50=22ms, p90=71ms, p95=98ms, p99=150ms, GPU util ~34%.
   Quick takeaway: quantization buys headroom on p99 while preserving latency at p50. Int8 reduces p99 roughly ~30% in this config.

2) Mixed-tenant noisy neighbor (70/20/10 split, same per-tenant qps proportional):
   - L-v1: p99 jumps to 860ms during transient microbursts from tenant B; mean queue length spikes 2.1x.
   - L-v1-q8: p99 ~520ms during same bursts; queue length smaller.
   - L-small serving fallback for tier-C reduces overall p99 for critical tenant to ~380ms by shedding load to small model.
   Notes: under mixed tenancy the kernel selection + scheduling matters more than raw model size. We observed that the runtime coalescer introduced ~6–8ms jitter on schedule boundaries — likely due to greedy batch formation under cross-tenant mixing.

3) Warm-cache vs cold-cache runs:
   - After priming (20k tokens), p99 drops ~15–20% vs cold run for all models. Effect largest on fp16 L-v1.
   - Suggestion: always prime hot-paths for expected traffic spikes; consider proactive cache priming for VIP customers.

4) Burst recovery behavior:
   - Under step increase from 250 -> 400 qps, L-v1 exhibits pronounced p99 tail beyond 1.2s for ~45s window. L-v1-q8 recovers to below 700ms in ~18s.
   - Observed pattern: queue length climbs nonlinearly as kernel selection attempts to inflate batch sizes; fallback policy not aggressive enough.

Simple ASCII charts from single run (L-v1 vs L-v1-q8 p99 over time):
   Time(min)  0    2    4    6    8   10
   L-v1 p99  430  470  880  620  390  430
   L-q8 p99  290  310  520  360  300  290

Hypotheses to test next (actionable):
- H1: Reducing max-batch-wait to 6ms during multi-tenant bursts will reduce p99 tail at expense of ~3% token/sec. Test + instrument.
- H2: More aggressive model-fallback (auto-route 15% of background traffic to L-small when queue>threshold) will keep VIP p99 < 350ms.
- H3: Enabling prefix-prefetch (warm priming) for predicted hot tokens reduces p99 by 10–25% for large models; cost model needed.

Planned experiments (short tasks):
- EXP-1: batch-wait sweep [2ms,4ms,6ms,8ms,12ms] on mixed-tenancy with L-v1-q8 (3 runs each). Owner: Soren. Target complete: 2024-11-22.
- EXP-2: fallback policy simulation (10%, 15%, 25% shed) with L-small as fallback. Owner: Aisha. Target complete: 2024-11-24.
- EXP-3: cache-priming budget vs benefit curve (prime tokens: 1k/5k/10k/20k). Owner: Evan. Target complete: 2024-11-26.

Open questions and unknowns:
- How much does RDMA vs NVLink placement affect q8 kernel latency? Need infra input.
- Is the observed 6–8ms coalescer jitter fixable by precomputing batch slots? Seems like a scheduler implementation detail.
- Pricing implication: L-v1-q8 is cheaper-per-token in practice but we need concrete cost model: GPU-hours + memory footprint + expected scale multiplier.

Notes to presenter (short bullets):
- Message: "Quantization provides robust p99 improvements for mixed tenancy and buys recovery time in bursts; combine with targeted fallback for predictable SLOs."
- Bring 2x slides: single-tenant p99 comparison, mixed-tenant burst timeline with fallback enabled.
- Have a short demo: run the 2-minute mixed-tenancy script with L-small fallback on stage.

Appendix: raw interesting snippets from metrics (copied):
- L-v1-q8 run-id r_20241115_01: p95 160ms p99 290ms; max queue 84; mean GPU util 59%.
- L-v1 run-id r_20241115_02: p95 210ms p99 430ms; max queue 132; mean GPU util 72%.

TODOs (immediate):
- [ ] Run EXP-1 and upload metrics to metrics/exp1-1119.json (Soren)
- [ ] Draft 2 slides for bakeoff; include cost delta table (Aisha)
- [ ] File follow-up infra task re: scheduler jitter (RT-3145) (Evan)

Small footnote: these are notebook-level numbers, runs not re-seeded except where noted. Use them to guide prioritization not as final claims.

End of scratchpad.

-- Soren
